digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest event storage
propositions: Physical deletion of committed UUID events reclaims no repository space from the git pack but breaks cross-clone merges via git rename detection pairing shared deletes with distinct new files per clone.

Read cost is asymmetric: digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest is already O(1) with single file open per ticket, but overlap/queue.py::_events_of opens and parses every matching file, causing pending_enrichment scan at 404+ ms against a 20 ms budget.

The suffix-lazy reader design bounds queue reduction to one open per event type per ticket plus k fallback opens on corruption, and claim arbitration to c opens where c is the number of claims in the current epoch, with no term depending on total history.
Merge-safe retention must rename to deterministic source-derived paths with identical content; physical prune with fresh UUIDs violates this rule and breaks reconvergence.
The design is read-only with no deletion, rename, or write, so it preserves invariant I1 and leaves two-clone reconvergence behavior unchanged.
